rationale: Acceptance is fully clean (11 pass, 1 correctly na) and standards adjudication found no concrete security issue, but the blind lens surfaced one real regression: the nginx /api block forwards the client Host instead of mirroring the Vite dev proxy's changeOrigin, so backend-generated absolute URLs differ between fast mode and the dev server and resolve to the SPA fallback in fast mode. The edge-case lens failed to return usable output across two dispatch attempts, so coverage is partial and confidence is forced to low. 11 of 12 blind concerns were dismissed as refuted or below the emission floor (notably the %VITE_SUFFIX% guard and the WebSocket and .env-secret concerns, each disproved against the repo); 0 findings deferred.

findings.title: Proxy Host header diverges from Vite dev proxy
findings.problem: The /api block sets proxy_set_header Host $host, forwarding the client's Host (localhost:5173). The Vite dev proxy it is meant to approximate uses changeOrigin: true against target http://localhost:8080, which rewrites Host to localhost:8080. The backend derives client-facing absolute URLs from that header, and the block's own comment documents only the percent-encoding divergence, not this one.
findings.impact: In fast mode, codemie/src/codemie/rest_api/routers/files.py:357 builds file_url from http_request.base_url.netloc, yielding http://localhost:5173/v1/files/<id>. That path carries no /api prefix, so nginx matches location / and try_files returns index.html instead of the file; under the dev server the same code yields http://localhost:8080/v1/files/<id>, which is reachable because the backend publishes 8080:8080. codemie/src/codemie/rest_api/a2a/utils.py:252 builds an agent-card URL the same way. Fast mode is therefore not a faithful substitute for the dev server: a green fast run can mask a real defect, or a test touching server-generated URLs can fail only in fast mode and look flaky.
findings.recommendation: Mirror the dev proxy explicitly with proxy_set_header Host localhost:8080; so backend-generated absolute URLs match dev-server behavior and stay reachable from the host browser. Optionally also set X-Forwarded-Proto and X-Forwarded-Host. Then re-run any sanity-ui test that exercises server-generated file URLs, and extend the block's divergence comment to cover Host handling.
